intro: A tokenizer may report character spans while a storage format uses byte positions. A boundary map translates between these coordinate systems without decoding arbitrary partial bytes.
task: Return the byte offset of every Unicode code point boundary, including the final boundary.
requirements: Return integer UTF-8 byte offsets for every Python code-point boundary, starting at zero and ending at len(text.encode("utf-8")). Unicode surrogate code points are invalid. Empty text returns [0].
Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Accumulate each character’s encoded byte length.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Include the final boundary so a span ending at the text end can be converted.

explanation: A tokenizer may report character spans while a storage format uses byte positions. A boundary map translates between these coordinate systems without decoding arbitrary partial bytes.
Code points are not grapheme clusters: a letter plus a combining mark has two boundaries here. UTF-8 characters occupy between one and four bytes, so multiplying by a fixed width is incorrect.
